title: Per-customer policy automation for batching & caching with safe apply/rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated, per-customer and per-route policy engine that recommends and safely applies batching and KV-caching configurations, supports allowlists/denylists for routes and customers, and enforces tier-based controls with auditable rollback. This ticket implements the controller and safe-apply lifecycle (validate -> dry-run -> canary -> full-rollout -> auto-rollback) and integrates with Console for visibility and manual overrides.

Motivation: Current cost optimization work is manual and coarse-grained. Customers with heterogeneous workloads (short chat vs long-form generation vs embedding-heavy routes) get suboptimal batching/kv policies, leading to unnecessary spend or latency regressions. We need per-customer segmentation, a flexible allowlist/denylist mechanism, and tier-aware defaults (free/dev/prod) so recommendations respect SLAs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy engine can ingest aggregated telemetry (p50/p95 latency, token/sec, request size distribution) and produce a recommended config for batching window, max batch size, and KV cache TTL per route and per-customer.
- Safe-apply lifecycle implemented with dry-run mode that simulates cost/latency impact and stores results in rollout history.
- Canary rollout supports percent-based targeting (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automatic rollback if specified SLOs breach or error rates increase by >2x baseline.
- Allowlist/denylist rules can be attached to customers, routes, or account tiers; denylist blocks automated changes, allowlist opts-in to aggressive batching.
- Console shows per-recommendation rationale, estimated monthly savings, confidence score, and links to telemetry that drove the recommendation.
- Audit logs and config versioning persisted and exportable; security review checklist passed.

Technical approach:
- Recommendation model: lightweight rule-based + heuristics engine using workload histograms (seq length, inter-arrival times) and a small ML score that estimates cost/latency tradeoffs. Implement as a microservice behind policy-api.
- Safe apply: extend existing rollout service to accept PolicyChange objects (immutable versions). Implement dry-run by replaying sampled traces through the runtime simulator (existing sandbox hooks).
- Canary & monitoring: wire rollout to tracing + metrics (per-customer token cost, p50/p95 latency, err rate). Define automatic rollback triggers and cooldown windows.
- Allowlist/denylist & tiers: store rules in Config Store with precedence (explicit deny > explicit allow > tier default). Expose an SDK check for runtime to honor denylist immediately on request path.
- Observability: Console integration to surface recommendation lineage (which traces/histograms triggered it), simulate projected savings, and allow manual approve/reject.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect recommendations causing latency regression: mitigate with conservative defaults, low initial canary % and strict rollback triggers.
- Overlapping rules (customer + route + tier): implement deterministic precedence and conflict-resolution policy documented in Console.
- High volume of per-customer policies increasing control-plane load: batch evaluation jobs and cache policy decisions in Redis with TTL tied to workload change detection.

Rollout plan:
1) Backend prototype w/ dry-run and simulated results (internal only).
2) Console UI mock and PM/Design review.
3) Small external canary: 5 customers that opt-in (allowlist).
4) Gradual expansion with monitoring gates and automated rollback.
